blocks.text: Overview

blocks.raw: # Core Concepts
blocks.text: Core Concepts

blocks.raw: ## What is a Search Filter?
blocks.text: What is a Search Filter?

blocks.raw: A **search filter** is a set of one or more indexed fields used to quickly look up data. You define which fields to search on—this setup is called the **search filter** .
blocks.text: A search filter is a set of one or more indexed fields used to quickly look up data. You define which fields to search on—this setup is called the search filter .

blocks.raw: There are two types of filters:
blocks.text: There are two types of filters:

blocks.raw:
* **AND filter** – Returns results only when *all* the conditions are met
* **OR filter** – Returns results when *any* of the conditions are met (available only for the **Customer** entity)
blocks.text: AND filter – Returns results only when all the conditions are metOR filter – Returns results when any of the conditions are met (available only for the Customer entity)

blocks.raw: Once the filter is set, the system knows how to query the database efficiently. You can then use the [Search API](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/perform-search) to fetch the results.
blocks.text: Once the filter is set, the system knows how to query the database efficiently. You can then use the Search API to fetch the results.

blocks.raw: # Key Features
blocks.text: Key Features

blocks.raw:
* Define the fields to search on—including custom and extended fields
* Set the time range for the data you want to query
* Supports **partial search** (starts with) for customer records
* Works across multiple languages
* Compatible with the **[Vulcan]()** UI framework (but not limited to it)
* Choose which fields appear in the search results; use **[Neo](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/extension)** for advanced customization

blocks.raw: ## Understanding Cardinality
blocks.text: Understanding Cardinality

blocks.raw: When creating a search filter, the system first checks the **cardinality** of the fields you've selected. Filters with **high cardinality** are more likely to pass validation and be activated.
blocks.text: When creating a search filter, the system first checks the cardinality of the fields you've selected. Filters with high cardinality are more likely to pass validation and be activated.

blocks.raw:
* **High Cardinality** means the field (or combination of fields) has a large number of unique values. This makes it a strong candidate for indexing and searching.\
  *Example:* `Bill number`—each value is likely unique.

* **Low Cardinality** means the field has only a few unique values. These fields aren’t ideal for filtering on their own.\
  *Example:* `Gender`—only a handful of values like Male, Female, Other. A filter with only this field will likely fail validation.

blocks.raw:
👉 **Note:** Cardinality is calculated based on all **mandatory fields** in your filter.\
The filter must pass the **cardinality check** before it can be activated.

blocks.raw: ### Note for customer search in new MemberCare
blocks.text: Note for customer search in new MemberCare

blocks.raw: Customer visibility in the new MemberCare depends on how the customer was registered and when the Cortex sync runs.
blocks.text: Customer visibility in the new MemberCare depends on how the customer was registered and when the Cortex sync runs.

blocks.raw:
* **Import Framework registrations**
  Customers registered through the Import Framework are not available for search immediately. Search feature requires a scheduled sync to make these customers searchable.

* **API-based registrations**
  Customers registered through APIs are synced to the Search in real time through event notifications. You can search for these customers immediately in the new MemberCare.

* **Search sync schedule**
  Search runs a daily sync at **12:00 AM (cluster timezone)**.
  For the **seacrm cluster (JST)**, the customer will be searchable after **8:30 PM IST** on the same day, once the sync completes.

blocks.raw: ## Search auto-enable for new orgs
blocks.text: Search auto-enable for new orgs

blocks.raw: When a new org is created, the system automatically enables search and creates a default search criteria. No manual configuration or Jira ticket is required.
blocks.text: When a new org is created, the system automatically enables search and creates a default search criteria. No manual configuration or Jira ticket is required.

blocks.raw: > **Note:** If your org was created before this feature was introduced, search is not enabled by default. Raise a Jira ticket to the sustenance team to enable it and set up a search criteria.
blocks.text: Note: If your org was created before this feature was introduced, search is not enabled by default. Raise a Jira ticket to the sustenance team to enable it and set up a search criteria.

blocks.raw: During org creation, the system does the following automatically:
blocks.text: During org creation, the system does the following automatically:

blocks.raw:
1. Enables search for the org. Config key `262` (search type) is set to enabled.
2. Creates a default [prefix (OR) search criteria](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-search-filter) for the `CUSTOMER` entity. The criteria supports searching by full name, email, external ID, or phone number.
blocks.text: Enables search for the org. Config key 262 (search type) is set to enabled.Creates a default prefix (OR) search criteria for the CUSTOMER entity. The criteria supports searching by full name, email, external ID, or phone number.

blocks.raw: Customers registered via API are immediately searchable in MemberCare using any of these fields.
blocks.text: Customers registered via API are immediately searchable in MemberCare using any of these fields.

blocks.raw: > **Note:** Customers registered through the Import Framework are not immediately searchable. They become available after the daily sync, which runs at 12:00 AM (cluster timezone).
blocks.text: Note: Customers registered through the Import Framework are not immediately searchable. They become available after the daily sync, which runs at 12:00 AM (cluster timezone).

blocks.raw: ### Customization options
blocks.text: Customization options

blocks.raw: The default criteria covers the most common search use cases. You can extend or replace it based on your org's requirements:
blocks.text: The default criteria covers the most common search use cases. You can extend or replace it based on your org's requirements:

blocks.raw:
* **Custom fields:** Add custom or extended fields to the search criteria using the [Create search filter API](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/create-meta-search).
* **Custom event transformation:** To modify how data is indexed before search (for example, stripping country codes from phone numbers), configure a [custom Neo event transformation](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/event-transformation-using-neo).
* **Additional criteria:** You can create up to two OR (prefix) criteria and up to five AND (combination) criteria per org for the `CUSTOMER` entity.

blocks.raw: ### Verifying search is enabled
blocks.text: Verifying search is enabled

blocks.raw: To confirm the auto-created search criteria, use the [Retrieve search criteria details API](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/get-meta). If search does not appear to be enabled for your org, raise a ticket to product support.
blocks.text: To confirm the auto-created search criteria, use the Retrieve search criteria details API. If search does not appear to be enabled for your org, raise a ticket to product support.

blocks.raw: The criteria shows as inactive for a few seconds after org creation. It becomes active automatically within a short time. No manual action is required.
